title: Write a function for a geometric quantity
subtitle: Nonlinear functions · 13 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **13 of the official questions in Nonlinear functions are this one** — 0 Easy, 5 Medium, 8 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The problem describes a shape whose dimensions depend on each other ('the length is 3 more than the width') and asks for a function giving the area or volume in terms of one named variable.
- The answer choices are expanded or factored polynomials.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Write every dimension in terms of the variable the question names.
- If the length is the input, the width is length − 3, not width + 3.
- 2) Multiply the dimensions using the formula for the shape.
- 3) Compare with the answer choices, expanding only if they are expanded.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Pick a test value for the variable, work out the true volume by hand, and evaluate each answer choice at that value to see which one matches.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You write the function in terms of the wrong dimension (width instead of length), so the offset has the wrong sign.
You also forget to multiply by the fixed height, or add the dimensions when you should multiply them.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You write the function in terms of the wrong dimension (width instead of length), so the offset has the wrong sign.
You also forget to multiply by the fixed height, or add the dimensions when you should multiply them.
